q: Which of the following is typically part of a test plan?
o: The test approach, including test levels, test types, test techniques and entry and exit criteria
Detailed defect reports with steps to reproduce
The root cause analysis of production failures
Test logs from the previous release
e: Contenido típico: contexto, supuestos y restricciones, stakeholders, comunicación, registro de riesgos, enfoque de prueba, presupuesto y calendario.

q: Which of the following is a purpose of a test plan?
o: It serves as a means of communication with team members and other stakeholders
It replaces the test strategy of the organization
It records the actual results of test execution
It lists all defects found in production
e: Un plan documenta medios y calendario, ayuda a cumplir los criterios, sirve para comunicarse y demuestra la adherencia a la política y estrategia de prueba (o explica las desviaciones).

q: How does test planning help testers, according to the syllabus?
o: It guides their thinking and forces them to confront future challenges related to risks, schedules, people, tools, costs and effort
It removes the need for test monitoring
It guarantees that the plan will never change
It ensures no defects will be found
e: Preparar el plan obliga a pensar en los retos futuros (riesgos, calendario, personas, herramientas, costes, esfuerzo).

q: In a test plan, where would you typically find hiring and training needs?
o: In the stakeholders section (roles, responsibilities, relevance to testing, hiring and training needs)
In the budget and schedule section
e: El syllabus sitúa las necesidades de contratación y formación dentro del apartado de stakeholders del plan.

q: Which standard provides more details about the test plan and its content?
e: La norma ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3 trata la documentación de pruebas, incluido el plan.

q: A test plan explains why testing will deviate from the organization's test strategy. Which purpose of the test plan does this serve?
o: Demonstrating that testing will adhere to the test policy and test strategy, or explaining why it will deviate from them
e: Uno de los propósitos del plan es demostrar la adherencia a la política y estrategia de prueba o explicar las desviaciones.

q: How does a tester typically contribute to release planning?
o: By participating in writing testable user stories and acceptance criteria, and in project and quality risk analyses
By breaking down user stories into coding tasks only
By deciding the release date alone
e: En release planning, los testers participan en escribir historias y criterios comprobables, en análisis de riesgos de proyecto y calidad, estiman esfuerzo, determinan el enfoque y planifican las pruebas de la release.

q: How does a tester typically contribute to iteration planning?
o: By participating in the detailed risk analysis of user stories and determining their testability
By deciding the order of all releases for the next year
e: En iteration planning, los testers analizan en detalle los riesgos de las historias, determinan su testabilidad, las dividen en tareas (sobre todo de prueba), estiman y refinan aspectos funcionales y no funcionales.

q: Which planning activity looks ahead to the end of a single iteration and is concerned with the iteration backlog?
e: La iteration planning mira al final de una iteración y trabaja con el backlog de la iteración; la release planning mira a la release y al product backlog.

q: Which statement about release planning is correct?
o: It serves as the basis for the test approach and test plan across all iterations
It only covers a single iteration
It is performed only by developers
It never involves refining user stories
e: La release planning define y redefine el product backlog, puede dividir historias grandes y es la base del enfoque y del plan de prueba de todas las iteraciones.

q: During iteration planning, testers break down user stories into:
e: Los testers dividen las historias en tareas (sobre todo de prueba) y estiman el esfuerzo de todas ellas.

q: In which kind of SDLC do release planning and iteration planning typically occur?
e: El syllabus indica que en ciclos de vida iterativos suelen darse dos tipos de planificación: de release y de iteración.

q: Which of the following is a typical EXIT criterion?
o: The planned level of coverage has been achieved and the number of unresolved defects is acceptable
e: Salida: medidas de exhaustividad (cobertura, defectos sin resolver, densidad, tests fallidos) y criterios sí/no. Requisitos disponibles, entorno listo y smoke tests superados son criterios de entrada.

q: Which of the following is a typical ENTRY criterion?
o: Availability of resources such as people, tools, environments and test data
e: Entrada: disponibilidad de recursos y testware, y nivel de calidad inicial del objeto de prueba (p. ej., smoke tests superados).

q: In Agile software development, what are exit criteria often called?
e: Los criterios de salida suelen llamarse Definition of Done; los criterios de entrada de una historia, Definition of Ready.

q: Under what circumstance can running out of time or budget be a valid exit criterion?
o: When stakeholders have reviewed and accepted the risk of going live without further testing
Never; testing must continue until all defects are fixed
Only if the testers decide so
e: Quedarse sin tiempo o presupuesto puede ser válido si los stakeholders aceptan el riesgo de salir sin más pruebas.

q: What is likely to happen if entry criteria are not met?
o: The activity will likely prove more difficult, time-consuming, costly and riskier
Nothing; entry criteria are only informative
e: El syllabus advierte que, sin cumplir los criterios de entrada, la actividad será probablemente más difícil, larga, cara y arriesgada.

q: Which statement about entry and exit criteria is correct?
o: They should be defined for each test level and will differ based on the test objectives
They are the same for every test level
They are defined only after testing has finished
e: Los criterios de entrada y salida deben definirse para cada nivel y difieren según los objetivos.

q: What does the test pyramid model suggest?
o: Many small, fast, isolated tests at the lower layers and fewer, slower, end-to-end tests at the higher layers
Most automated tests should be end-to-end tests through the UI
All layers should contain the same number of tests
Lower-layer tests are slower and more expensive than higher-layer tests
e: Cuanto más alta la capa: menos granularidad, menos aislamiento y más tiempo de ejecución. Abajo hacen falta muchos tests; arriba, pocos.

q: Which three layers does the original test pyramid model by Cohn define?
o: Unit tests, service tests and UI tests
Component tests, system tests and acceptance tests
Static tests, dynamic tests and manual tests
Smoke tests, regression tests and exploratory tests
e: El modelo original (Cohn 2009) define unit, service y UI tests. Otro modelo popular usa unit, integration y end-to-end.

q: In the test pyramid, what happens as you move to a higher layer?
o: Test granularity and isolation decrease, and test execution time increases
Test granularity increases and execution time decreases
Tests become more isolated and faster
The number of tests needed increases
e: Más arriba: menor granularidad, menor aislamiento (más dependencia de otros elementos) y más tiempo de ejecución.

q: How does the test pyramid support the team?
o: In test automation and test effort allocation, by showing that different test objectives are supported by different levels of automation
By defining the order of test levels in a sequential model
By determining the risk level of each test
e: La pirámide apoya la automatización y la asignación de esfuerzo mostrando que distintos objetivos se cubren con distintos niveles de automatización.

q: Which statement about the layers of the test pyramid is correct?
o: The number and naming of the layers may differ between models
There must always be exactly three layers named unit, integration and UI
The top layer must contain the most tests
The layers correspond to the seven testing principles
e: El número y el nombre de las capas pueden variar; también pueden usarse otros niveles de prueba.

q: Tests in the bottom layer of the test pyramid are typically:
o: Small, isolated, fast, and check a small piece of functionality
Slow tests that need the whole system deployed
e: Los tests de la base son pequeños, aislados y rápidos, y comprueban una pieza pequeña, así que se necesitan muchos.

q: In the testing quadrants model, which quadrant contains technology-facing tests that critique the product, such as non-functional tests (except usability) and smoke tests?
e: Q1: técnicos, apoyan al equipo (componente e integración de componentes). Q2: de negocio, apoyan al equipo (funcionales, ejemplos, historias, prototipos UX, API, simulaciones). Q3: de negocio, critican el producto (exploratoria, usabilidad, UAT). Q4: técnicos, critican el producto (smoke y no funcionales salvo usabilidad).

q: Which quadrant contains component tests and component integration tests that should be automated and included in the CI process?
e: Q1 = orientado a la tecnología y de apoyo al equipo: pruebas de componente e integración de componentes, automatizadas y en CI.

q: Exploratory testing, usability testing and user acceptance testing belong to which quadrant?
e: Q3 agrupa las pruebas orientadas al usuario que critican el producto, a menudo manuales: exploratoria, usabilidad y UAT.

q: Functional tests, examples, user story tests, user experience prototypes, API testing and simulations belong to which quadrant?
e: Q2 comprueba los criterios de aceptación y puede ser manual o automatizado.

q: Which two viewpoints combine to form the four testing quadrants?
o: Business facing vs technology facing, and support the team vs critique the product
Manual vs automated, and static vs dynamic
Functional vs non-functional, and black-box vs white-box
Early vs late, and cheap vs expensive
e: Los cuadrantes combinan dos ejes: orientado a negocio o a tecnología, y apoyo al equipo o crítica del producto.

q: Who defined the testing quadrants referenced in the syllabus?
e: Los cuadrantes los definió Brian Marick (Marick 2003, Crispin 2008). La pirámide de pruebas es de Cohn.

q: Usability testing appears in which quadrant?
e: La usabilidad está en Q3; Q4 contiene las no funcionales excepto la usabilidad.

q: How do the testing quadrants support test management?
o: They help visualize that all appropriate test types and test levels are included in the SDLC
They define the exact number of test cases per sprint
They determine the order of test execution
e: El modelo ayuda a visualizar que se incluyen todos los tipos y niveles de prueba adecuados, y que algunos tipos son más relevantes en ciertos niveles.

q: Tests in which quadrant check the acceptance criteria and can be manual or automated?
e: Los tests de Q2 (de negocio, apoyo al equipo) comprueban los criterios de aceptación.

q: In the testing quadrants, what does "critique the product" mean?
o: The tests measure the product's behavior against the expectations
The tests are written by critics outside the team
e: "Support the team" = guiar el desarrollo; "critique the product" = medir el comportamiento frente a las expectativas.

q: Risk level is determined by:
o: Number of test cases and test coverage
Number of testers and project budget
e: El nivel de riesgo combina la probabilidad de que ocurra con el impacto (daño) si ocurre.

q: How is risk likelihood defined in the syllabus?
o: The probability of the risk occurrence, greater than zero and less than one
The consequences of the risk occurrence
The cost of mitigating the risk
The number of times the risk has occurred before
e: La probabilidad del riesgo está entre 0 y 1 (excluidos); el impacto es el daño o las consecuencias.

q: What is a risk, according to the syllabus?
o: A potential event, hazard, threat or situation whose occurrence causes an adverse effect
A defect that has already been found
A test case with high priority
e: Un riesgo es un evento, peligro, amenaza o situación potencial cuya ocurrencia causa un efecto adverso.

q: What does the risk level indicate?
o: The higher the risk level, the more important is its treatment
The higher the risk level, the less testing is needed
The risk level only matters for project risks
The risk level is the number of affected requirements
e: El nivel de riesgo es una medida: cuanto mayor, más importante su tratamiento.

q: Risk impact is also known as:
e: El syllabus define el impacto del riesgo (harm) como las consecuencias de su ocurrencia.

q: Two risks have the same likelihood. Risk A would cause minor cosmetic issues; risk B would cause financial loss for customers. Which statement is correct?
o: Risk B has a higher risk level because its impact is higher
Both risks have the same risk level because their likelihood is the same
Risk A has a higher risk level because it is more visible
Risk level cannot be compared without counting test cases
e: Con la misma probabilidad, el riesgo de mayor impacto tiene mayor nivel de riesgo.

q: Which of the following is a PROJECT risk?
o: The delivery of the test environment is delayed
The user interface is difficult to use
The application contains a security vulnerability
e: Los riesgos de proyecto afectan a la gestión y el control: organizativos, de personas, técnicos y de proveedores. Los otros son riesgos de producto.

q: Which of the following is a PRODUCT risk?
o: Inadequate response time of the system
e: Los riesgos de producto están ligados a las características de calidad: funcionalidad, cálculos, errores en tiempo de ejecución, arquitectura, algoritmos, tiempo de respuesta, experiencia de usuario, seguridad.

q: Scope creep and poor tool support are examples of which kind of risk?
e: Ampliación descontrolada del alcance y mal soporte de herramientas son riesgos de proyecto de tipo técnico.

q: What may happen when project risks occur?
o: They may impact the project schedule, budget or scope
They directly cause failures in production
They only affect the test team
e: Los riesgos de proyecto pueden afectar al calendario, al presupuesto o al alcance, y por tanto a la capacidad de cumplir objetivos.

q: Which of the following is a possible consequence of a product risk occurring?
o: User dissatisfaction and loss of revenue, trust or reputation
A delay in the test environment delivery
e: Consecuencias de riesgos de producto: insatisfacción del usuario, pérdida de ingresos o reputación, daños a terceros, altos costes de mantenimiento, sanciones penales e incluso daños físicos.

q: Communication problems and conflicts within the team are examples of:
o: Project risks related to people issues
e: Son riesgos de proyecto de tipo "personas": habilidades insuficientes, conflictos, problemas de comunicación, falta de personal.

q: What does product risk analysis consist of?
e: El análisis de riesgos = identificación + evaluación. El control de riesgos = mitigación + monitorización.

q: How can the results of product risk analysis influence testing?
o: They are used to determine the test scope, test levels, test types, test techniques and coverage to be achieved
They are used only to decide the release date
They replace the need for test planning
They determine which developer must fix each defect
e: Los resultados determinan alcance, niveles y tipos, técnicas y cobertura, esfuerzo, priorización y otras actividades además de las pruebas.

q: In the quantitative approach to risk assessment, how is the risk level calculated?
o: As the multiplication of risk likelihood and risk impact
As the sum of all identified risks
As the number of test cases per risk
e: Cuantitativo: nivel = probabilidad × impacto. Cualitativo: se usa una matriz de riesgos.

q: Which technique can stakeholders use to identify risks?
o: Brainstorming, workshops, interviews or cause-effect diagrams
e: El syllabus menciona lluvia de ideas, talleres, entrevistas y diagramas causa-efecto.

q: What is the goal of product risk analysis from a testing perspective?
o: To provide awareness of product risk so that test effort is focused to minimize residual product risk
To eliminate all product risks before testing starts
To avoid testing low-risk areas completely
To replace the test plan with a risk register
e: El objetivo es enfocar el esfuerzo de prueba para minimizar el riesgo residual del producto, idealmente empezando pronto en el ciclo de vida.

q: Why is categorization of identified risks useful in risk assessment?
o: Risks in the same category can usually be mitigated using a similar approach
Categorized risks do not need to be tested
Only categorized risks can be reported
e: Categorizar ayuda a asignar acciones de mitigación, porque los riesgos de una misma categoría suelen mitigarse de forma parecida.

q: Which of the following is an example of mitigating product risks through testing?
o: Applying the appropriate test techniques and coverage levels for the risk
Buying insurance against the consequences of the risk
Accepting the risk without further action
Preparing a contingency plan for when the risk occurs
e: Mitigación por pruebas: testers adecuados, nivel de independencia apropiado, revisiones y análisis estático, técnicas y cobertura apropiadas, tipos de prueba adecuados y prueba dinámica (incluida regresión).

q: Purchasing insurance to cover the consequences of a product risk is an example of:
e: Opciones de respuesta: mitigación por pruebas, aceptación, transferencia o plan de contingencia. Un seguro transfiere el riesgo.

q: What is the aim of risk monitoring?
o: To ensure that mitigation actions are effective, obtain information to improve risk assessment and identify emerging risks
To identify risks for the first time
To calculate the cost of testing
To decide which developer caused the risk
e: La monitorización comprueba la eficacia de la mitigación, mejora la evaluación e identifica riesgos emergentes.

q: What does product risk control consist of?
e: El control de riesgos de producto = mitigación + monitorización.

q: Which action is a way to mitigate product risks by testing?
o: Applying an appropriate level of independence of testing
Removing regression tests to save time
Assigning the least experienced testers to the highest risks
e: Aplicar el nivel de independencia adecuado es una de las acciones de mitigación por pruebas.

q: A team decides to do nothing about a low-level product risk because the cost of mitigation outweighs the potential harm. Which response option is this?
e: Decidir no actuar ante un riesgo es aceptación del riesgo.

q: Which of the following is an example of a defect metric?
e: Métricas de defectos: número y prioridad de defectos encontrados/corregidos, densidad, porcentaje de detección. El tiempo medio hasta el fallo es de calidad de producto.

q: Requirements coverage and code coverage are examples of:
e: El syllabus clasifica la cobertura de requisitos y de código como métricas de cobertura.

q: Which of the following is a product quality metric?
e: Métricas de calidad de producto: disponibilidad, tiempo de respuesta, tiempo medio hasta el fallo.

q: Residual risk level is an example of which type of metric?
e: El nivel de riesgo residual es una métrica de riesgo.

q: Number of test cases run/not run and passed/failed are examples of:
e: Métricas de progreso de prueba: avance de implementación de casos, preparación del entorno, casos ejecutados/no ejecutados, superados/fallidos, tiempo de ejecución.

q: Why are test metrics gathered?
o: To show progress against the planned schedule and budget, the current quality of the test object and the effectiveness of test activities
e: Las métricas muestran el progreso frente a calendario y presupuesto, la calidad actual y la eficacia de las pruebas, y apoyan el control y el cierre.

q: Which content is typical of a test PROGRESS report?
o: Progress against the test plan, impediments and workarounds, metrics, new and changed risks, and the testing planned for the next period
The final evaluation of product quality against the exit criteria for the whole project
The archive of all testware at project end
e: El informe de progreso es periódico y apoya el control. La evaluación final, las lecciones aprendidas y los riesgos no mitigados van en el informe de finalización.

q: Which content is typical of a test COMPLETION report?
o: Unmitigated risks, defects not fixed and lessons learned relevant to the testing
Testing planned for the next period
The list of test cases to be executed tomorrow
e: Informe de finalización: resumen, evaluación frente al plan, desviaciones, impedimentos, métricas, riesgos no mitigados, defectos sin corregir y lecciones aprendidas.

q: When is a test completion report prepared?
o: During test completion, when a project, test level or test type is complete and, ideally, its exit criteria have been met
Only when a critical defect is found
e: Se prepara en el cierre, cuando termina un proyecto, nivel o tipo de prueba, idealmente cumplidos los criterios de salida.

q: How does the audience influence test reporting?
o: Different audiences require different information and influence the formality and frequency of reporting
All audiences must receive exactly the same report
Reports should only be sent to testers
e: Distintas audiencias necesitan información distinta: los informes de progreso dentro del equipo suelen ser frecuentes e informales; el de finalización sigue una plantilla y se hace una vez.

q: What is the main purpose of test progress reports?
o: To support ongoing test control by providing enough information to modify the schedule, resources or test plan when needed
e: Los informes de progreso apoyan el control continuo y deben permitir cambiar el calendario, los recursos o el plan cuando haga falta.

q: What does the ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3 standard call test progress reports?
e: La norma 29119-3 llama a los informes de progreso test status reports.

q: Which of the following is an option for communicating the status of testing?
o: Dashboards such as CI/CD dashboards, task boards and burn-down charts
e: Opciones: comunicación verbal, dashboards, canales electrónicos (email, chat), documentación online e informes formales. Pueden combinarse.

q: For which teams may more formal communication be more appropriate?
o: Distributed teams, where face-to-face communication is not always possible due to distance or time differences
Co-located teams working in the same room
Teams that do not use any tools
e: En equipos distribuidos, la comunicación más formal puede ser más adecuada por la distancia o las diferencias horarias.

q: How should the communication of test status be tailored?
o: To the stakeholders, since different stakeholders are interested in different types of information
It should be identical for all stakeholders
It should be decided only by the tool vendor
It should contain only raw test logs
e: Cada stakeholder se interesa por información distinta, así que la comunicación debe adaptarse.

q: In the case of self-organizing teams, who decides the best means of communicating test status?
e: El syllabus indica que, en equipos autoorganizados, el propio equipo decide el mejor medio.

q: Email and chat are examples of which option for communicating test status?
e: Email y chat son canales de comunicación electrónica.

q: Which statement about the means of communicating test status is correct?
o: One or more options can be used, and the best means depends on factors such as test management concerns and regulatory standards
Only one option may be used per project
Formal reports are always the best option
e: Se pueden combinar varias opciones; la mejor depende de la gestión de pruebas, la estrategia de la organización, la normativa o el propio equipo.

q: What is the main purpose of configuration management in testing?
o: To identify, control and track work products such as test plans, test cases and test results as configuration items
To configure the test environment's hardware
To decide which defects must be fixed before release
e: En testing, la gestión de la configuración es una disciplina para identificar, controlar y rastrear productos de trabajo como elementos de configuración.

q: What happens when a configuration item is approved for testing?
o: It becomes a baseline and can only be changed through a formal change control process
It can be freely modified by anyone
It is deleted from the repository
It is automatically released to production
e: Al aprobarse para pruebas, el elemento se convierte en línea base y solo puede cambiarse mediante un control de cambios formal.

q: How does configuration management help reproduce previous test results?
o: It keeps a record of changed items when a new baseline is created, making it possible to revert to a previous baseline
It stores only the latest version of each item
e: La gestión de la configuración registra los cambios al crear una nueva línea base y permite volver a una anterior para reproducir resultados.

q: For a complex configuration item such as a test environment, what does configuration management record?
o: The items it consists of, their relationships and versions
Only the name of the environment
Only the cost of the hardware
Only the names of the testers who used it
e: Para elementos complejos registra sus componentes, sus relaciones y sus versiones.

q: To properly support testing, configuration management ensures that:
o: All configuration items are uniquely identified, version controlled, tracked for changes and related to each other so that traceability can be maintained
All defects are fixed before release
All requirements are approved by management
e: Garantiza identificación única, control de versiones, seguimiento de cambios y relación entre elementos (trazabilidad), y que el testware referencie sin ambigüedad la documentación y el software.

q: Where is automated configuration management normally included?
o: In an automated DevOps pipeline implementing CI, continuous delivery and continuous deployment
Only in the test completion report
e: CI, entrega continua y despliegue continuo suelen implementarse en un pipeline DevOps automatizado, que normalmente incluye gestión de la configuración automatizada.

q: Which of the following are examples of work products managed as configuration items in testing?
o: Test plans, test strategies, test conditions, test cases, test scripts, test results, test logs and test reports
e: El syllabus enumera estos productos de prueba como posibles elementos de configuración.

q: What are "test items" in the context of configuration management?
o: Individual parts of the test object
e: El syllabus define los test items como partes individuales del objeto de prueba.

q: Which statement about the testware and configuration management is correct?
o: All identified documentation and software items should be referenced unambiguously in testware
Testware should never reference software versions
Testware is not subject to configuration management
Only automated tests need to be referenced
e: La gestión de la configuración garantiza que la documentación y el software identificados se referencien sin ambigüedad en el testware.

q: A tester cannot reproduce a failure reported last month because nobody knows which build and test data were used. Which practice would have prevented this?
e: La gestión de la configuración registra versiones y relaciones de los elementos (build, datos, entorno), lo que permite reproducir resultados anteriores.

q: Which of the following should NOT be included in a defect report?
o: An assessment of which developer is to blame for the defect
Steps to reproduce, with expected and actual results
Identification of the test object and test environment
e: Un informe contiene identificador, título, fecha, organización y autor, objeto y entorno, contexto, descripción para reproducir, resultado esperado y real, severidad, prioridad, estado y referencias. Buscar culpables no aporta nada.

q: A defect report states: "Title: Login fails. Steps: open app, log in. Result: error." Which essential information is MOST clearly missing to enable reproduction and resolution?
o: The expected result, the test data used and the identification of the test object version and environment
The name of the tester's manager
The tester's opinion about the developer
The planned release date of the next version
e: Para reproducir y resolver hacen falta el resultado esperado, los datos usados (usuario, contraseña) y la versión del objeto y el entorno. Las otras opciones no ayudan a resolver.

q: A defect causes a typo in a rarely visited help page, but the CEO wants it fixed before tomorrow's demo. How should severity and priority be set?
e: La severidad mide el impacto en stakeholders o requisitos (aquí bajo); la prioridad, la urgencia de corrección (aquí alta por la demo).

q: A defect corrupts customer data, but only in a feature that will not be released for six months. How should severity and priority typically be set?
o: Severity and priority cannot be set until it is fixed
e: El impacto (corrupción de datos) es alto, pero la urgencia es baja porque la funcionalidad no se publicará pronto.

q: Which of the following is an objective of a typical defect report?
o: Providing those responsible for handling the defect with sufficient information to resolve it
e: Objetivos: dar información suficiente para resolver, permitir seguir la calidad del producto y aportar ideas de mejora de los procesos.

q: A tester reported an anomaly, but analysis showed the test expected result was wrong. Which status is the most appropriate for the defect report?
e: Las anomalías reportadas pueden resultar no ser defectos (p. ej., un falso positivo). Rechazarlo es el estado adecuado. Ejemplos de estado: open, deferred, duplicate, waiting to be fixed, awaiting confirmation testing, re-opened, closed, rejected.

q: In which part of a defect report should you record "test case TC-112 was being executed using boundary value test data during system testing"?
e: El contexto incluye el caso de prueba ejecutado, la actividad, la fase del ciclo de vida y otra información relevante (técnica, checklist, datos).

q: Which of the following is the best title for a defect report?
o: Checkout: total ignores 10% discount code for orders over €100
Checkout is broken, developer did not test
Something is wrong with prices sometimes
e: El título debe resumir brevemente la anomalía. Las otras opciones son vagas o acusatorias.

q: A defect fix has been delivered and the report is waiting for the tester to verify it. Which status fits best?
e: Tras entregarse el arreglo, el informe queda pendiente de la prueba de confirmación antes de cerrarse.

q: A tester finds that a new defect report describes exactly the same anomaly as an existing open report. What should be done?
o: Mark the new report as a duplicate and reference the existing one
Increase the severity of the original report
e: Un informe duplicado se marca como tal y se referencia al existente; "duplicate" es uno de los estados citados en el syllabus.

In previous similar projects, the development-to-test effort ratio was 3:2. The development effort of the new project is estimated at 600 person-days. Using estimation based on ratios, what is the estimated test effort?
e: Esfuerzo de prueba = desarrollo × 2/3 = 600 × 2/3 = 400 días-persona (estimación basada en ratios, una técnica basada en métricas).

q: The test effort in the last three iterations was 30, 36 and 33 person-hours. Using extrapolation as the average of the last three iterations, what is the estimated test effort for the next iteration?
e: Extrapolación (media de las últimas tres iteraciones): (30 + 36 + 33) / 3 = 33 horas-persona.

q: So far, executing 40 test cases took 120 person-hours. 60 test cases remain, and they are of similar complexity. Using extrapolation from the data gathered in this project, how much effort will the remaining test cases need?
e: Ritmo medido: 120/40 = 3 h por caso. Restantes: 60 × 3 = 180 horas-persona.

q: So far, executing 25 test cases took 100 person-hours. 75 test cases remain, and they are of similar complexity. Using extrapolation from the data gathered in this project, how much effort will the remaining test cases need?
e: Ritmo medido: 100/25 = 4 h por caso. Restantes: 75 × 4 = 300 horas-persona.

q: So far, executing 50 test cases took 150 person-hours. 30 test cases remain, and they are of similar complexity. Using extrapolation from the data gathered in this project, how much effort will the remaining test cases need?
e: Ritmo medido: 150/50 = 3 h por caso. Restantes: 30 × 3 = 90 horas-persona.

q: Experts estimate the test effort in isolation. Estimates outside the agreed boundaries are discussed, and the experts estimate again in isolation until consensus is reached. Which estimation technique is this?
e: Wideband Delphi es una técnica iterativa basada en expertos; Planning Poker es una variante.

q: The test cases below must be executed in priority order, but a test case can only be executed after the test case it depends on. Which execution order is correct?
e: Se ejecuta primero la de mayor prioridad cuyas dependencias ya se hayan cumplido. Si una prueba de alta prioridad depende de otra de menor prioridad, esa otra debe ir antes. Resultado: TC2, TC4, TC5, TC1, TC3.
code:
Test case  Priority  Depends on
TC1        4         –
TC2        1         –
TC3        5         TC5
TC4        3         –
TC5        2         TC4
(priority 1 = highest)

q: Using additional coverage prioritization (the test with the highest coverage first, then each next test is the one adding the most additional coverage), which test is executed SECOND?
e: Primero va T2 (5 requisitos). Después, la que más cobertura adicional aporta es T3. Orden completo: T2, T3, T5, T1, T4.
code:
Test  Requirements covered
T1    R1, R2, R3, R4
T2    R1, R2, R3, R4, R5
T3    R6, R7
T4    R5, R6
T5    R8

q: Using risk-based prioritization with a quantitative risk level (likelihood × impact, scale 1–5), in which order should the tests be executed?
e: Nivel de riesgo = probabilidad × impacto: T1 = 5×4 = 20, T2 = 4×2 = 8, T3 = 1×5 = 5, T4 = 4×3 = 12. Se ejecuta de mayor a menor: T1, T4, T2, T3.
code:
Test  Likelihood  Impact
T1    5           4
T2    4           2
T3    1           5
T4    4           3
